mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the monetary cycle supports risk asset performance.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window, or 20-day returns in low-rate periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as economic weakness triggers risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0%, or the correlation between UNRATE rise and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Joint growth in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% in the prior 3 months indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both > 0.5% change in 3 months
evidence_refs: fact:Retail sales and housing starts at 449904 and 1149.0 in January 2016
failure_condition: The joint signal fails when RSAFS and HOUST both exceed 0.5% growth but 60-day SPX returns are negative in > 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monetary tightening cycle defined by FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 2.0% increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:2016 FEDFUNDS at 0.34% and CPIAUCSL at 237.847
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 60% of instances meeting the trigger condition, or the signal's Rank IC is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals expanding labor market conditions, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as business confidence rises.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year window, or 5-day returns in high PAYEMS growth periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 indicates weakening manufacturing activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as supply chain disruptions reduce corporate earnings.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 fails to predict negative returns when SPX returns are positive in > 60% of such cases, or the correlation is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A late-cycle expansion regime defined by HOUST > 1200 and RSAFS > 450000 signals economic overheating, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as central banks accelerate tightening.
evidence_refs: fact:HOUST at 1149.0 and RSAFS at 449904.0 in January 2016
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 60% of instances meeting the trigger condition, or the signal's predictive power is not significant (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Joint growth in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP (GDPC1) exceeding 0.5% in the prior 3 months indicates synchronized supply and demand expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and GDPC1 both > 0.5% change in 3 months
evidence_refs: fact:INDPRO at 106.0222 and GDPC1 at 16442.3 in January 2016
failure_condition: The interaction signal fails when both INDPRO and GDPC1 exceed 0.5% growth but 5-day SPX returns are negative in > 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression is not significant (p > 0.05).
